items.q: A 29-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and 2 years of primary infertility seeks ovulation induction. Her husband's semen analysis is normal, and an HSG demonstrates patent fallopian tubes. What is the first-line medical therapy to induce ovulation?
items.exp: The landmark NICHD PPCOS II trial and current international ESHRE/ASRM guidelines establish letrozole (aromatase inhibitor, 2.5 mg to 7.5 mg daily for 5 days) as the first-line ovulation induction agent for anovulatory women with PCOS. It achieves significantly higher live birth and ovulation rates compared to clomiphene citrate without endometrial thinning.
r: Correct. Letrozole is the established first-line ovulation induction agent in PCOS with superior live birth rates.
Incorrect. Clomiphene citrate was historically first-line but is now second-line due to anti-estrogenic endometrial effects.
Incorrect. Metformin monotherapy is inferior to letrozole for inducing ovulation and live births.
Incorrect. Gonadotropins are second-line after oral agent failure due to costs and multiple gestation risks.
items.kp: Letrozole is the first-line medication for ovulation induction in women with anovulatory PCOS.

items.q: Which investigation provides the most reliable confirmation of ovulation in a woman with regular 28-day menstrual cycles?
o: Serum progesterone measured on day 21 of the cycle
items.exp: A mid-luteal serum progesterone level measured 7 days before anticipated menses (day 21 in a typical 28-day cycle) exceeding 30 nmol/L (or > 10 ng/mL) provides definitive, objective laboratory confirmation of active luteal corpus luteum function and ovulation.
r: Correct. Day 21 serum progesterone > 30 nmol/L confirms active corpus luteum secretory function and ovulation.
Incorrect. Basal body temperature shows biphasic shift retrospectively but is subjective and prone to error.
Incorrect. Day 14 estradiol reflects follicular maturation, not actual follicle rupture.
Incorrect. LH surge predicts impending ovulation within 24-36 hours but does not confirm luteinization or follicle rupture.
items.kp: Mid-luteal serum progesterone measured on day 21 (> 30 nmol/L or > 10 ng/mL) is the gold standard for confirming ovulation.

items.q: According to the World Health Organization (WHO 2021, 6th edition) laboratory manual, what is the lower reference limit for total sperm motility in a normal semen analysis?
items.exp: Under the WHO 2021 (6th edition) semen analysis manual guidelines, the fifth percentile lower reference limits are: semen volume 1.4 mL, sperm concentration 16 million/mL, total motility 42% (or progressive motility 30%), and normal forms 4.0%.
r: Correct. WHO 2021 establishes >= 42% total motility and >= 30% progressive motility as lower reference limits.
Incorrect. 60% exceeds the standard 5th percentile reference cutoff.
Incorrect. 25% represents significant asthenozoospermia.
Incorrect. 15% reflects severe motility impairment.
items.kp: WHO 2021 semen analysis lower reference limits require >= 42% total motility (>= 30% progressive motility) and >= 4% normal forms.

items.q: Which biomarker of ovarian reserve remains stable throughout the menstrual cycle and can be measured on any random cycle day?
items.exp: Anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) is secreted continuously by granulosa cells of gonadotropin-independent preantral and small antral follicles. Because these follicles develop continuously, serum AMH exhibits minimal intracycle variation and can be sampled on any day of the menstrual cycle.
r: Correct. AMH has minimal intracycle variability and reflects the functional primordial follicle pool on any cycle day.
Incorrect. FSH fluctuates dramatically and must be measured specifically on cycle days 2 to 4.
Incorrect. Estradiol varies continuously across follicular and luteal phases.
Incorrect. LH exhibits pulsatile secretion and surges dramatically mid-cycle.
items.kp: Anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) reflects ovarian reserve and can be measured on any day of the menstrual cycle.

items.q: A couple has been trying to conceive for 3 years. The husband's semen analysis shows a sperm concentration of 2 million/mL with 10% motility and 1% normal forms. The female partner has normal ovarian reserve and patent tubes. What is the treatment of choice?
o: Natural timed intercourse with LH kits
Clomiphene citrate therapy for the husband
items.exp: Severe oligoasthenoteratozoospermia (concentration < 5 million/mL, low motility, low normal morphology) carries an extremely low probability of conception with timed intercourse or IUI (which requires >= 5-10 million motile sperm). Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is the treatment of choice.
r: Correct. ICSI directly bypasses severe male factor defects by injecting a single selected spermatozoon into each mature oocyte.
Incorrect. IUI requires a post-wash total motile sperm count > 5-10 million to achieve acceptable pregnancy rates.
Incorrect. Timed intercourse has a near-zero success rate in severe OAT.
Incorrect. Clomiphene for the male has unproven efficacy and delays definitive treatment.
items.kp: Severe male factor subfertility (concentration < 5 million/mL) is the primary clinical indication for ICSI.

items.q: What is the most severe and potentially life-threatening complication of controlled ovarian hyperstimulation during in vitro fertilization?
items.exp: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) is an iatrogenic, potentially fatal complication triggered by hCG administration in the presence of numerous stimulated follicles. Excessive ovarian release of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) causes massive third-space capillary fluid extravasation, ascites, pleural effusion, hemoconcentration, and thrombosis.
r: Correct. Severe OHSS causes massive third-spacing, hypovolemia, hemoconcentration, and life-threatening thromboembolism.
Incorrect. Pelvic infection is rare following sterile transvaginal oocyte retrieval.
Incorrect. Ectopic pregnancy is a complication of embryo transfer, but less acutely life-threatening than severe OHSS.
Incorrect. Multiple gestation is common with multiple embryo transfer, but not an acute physiological crisis like OHSS.
items.kp: Severe OHSS is mediated by excessive VEGF release leading to massive capillary hyperpermeability and thrombosis.

items.q: A hysterosalpingogram (HSG) in a 32-year-old infertile woman demonstrates bilateral dilated fallopian tubes with a retort-shaped appearance and absence of free peritoneal contrast spill. What is the diagnosis?
o: Tubal spasm at the uterotubal junction
items.exp: A dilated, fluid-filled, retort-shaped fallopian tube with failure of peritoneal contrast spill is characteristic of hydrosalpinx, typically resulting from distal fimbrial occlusion secondary to prior pelvic inflammatory disease. Hydrosalpinges contain toxic fluid that reduces IVF implantation by 50% unless clipped or removed.
r: Correct. Bilateral distension with distal blockage and absent peritoneal spill defines hydrosalpinx.
Incorrect. Tubal spasm causes proximal abrupt non-filling at the cornu, not distal ballooning.
Incorrect. Salpingitis isthmica nodosa causes multiple small diverticular outpouchings in the isthmus.
Incorrect. Polyps produce filling defects within the uterine cavity, not tubal distension.
items.kp: Hydrosalpinx presents on HSG as distal tubal ballooning without peritoneal spill and should be removed before IVF.

items.q: Which strategy is most effective for preventing ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) in high-responder patients undergoing IVF?
o: GnRH agonist trigger instead of hCG trigger with a freeze-all embryo strategy
Double dose of urinary hCG for final oocyte maturation
Immediate transfer of fresh cleavage-stage embryos
items.exp: In GnRH antagonist stimulation protocols, substituting a GnRH agonist trigger (leuprolide) for the traditional hCG trigger eliminates sustained LH-receptor stimulation, rapidly collapsing VEGF secretion. Combining this with elective cryopreservation of all embryos ('freeze-all' strategy) completely prevents late-onset pregnancy-induced OHSS.
r: Correct. GnRH agonist trigger and elective cryopreservation of all embryos effectively eliminates severe OHSS.
Incorrect. Increasing the hCG dose dramatically worsens OHSS risk.
Incorrect. Oral progesterone has no impact on VEGF-mediated vascular permeability.
Incorrect. Fresh embryo transfer risks pregnancy, which produces endogenous hCG and triggers severe late OHSS.
items.kp: A GnRH agonist trigger combined with a 'freeze-all' embryo strategy prevents ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome in high responders.

items.q: What is the physiological mechanism by which clomiphene citrate induces ovulation?
o: Competitive antagonism of hypothalamic estrogen receptors, disinhibiting GnRH and FSH pulsatility
Direct agonism of ovarian follicle-stimulating hormone receptors
items.exp: Clomiphene citrate is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that binds and competitively blocks estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus. This prevents circulating estrogen from exerting negative feedback, misleading the brain into perceiving a hypoestrogenic state and triggering compensatory pulsatile release of GnRH and pituitary FSH.
r: Correct. Clomiphene blocks hypothalamic estrogen receptors, triggering increased GnRH and pituitary FSH secretion.
Incorrect. It has no direct action on ovarian FSH receptors.
Incorrect. It does not suppress adrenal androgen production.
Incorrect. It does not inhibit prolactin; dopamine agonists treat hyperprolactinemia.
items.kp: Clomiphene blocks hypothalamic estrogen receptors to increase GnRH and pituitary FSH pulsatility.

items.q: A 38-year-old woman with diminished ovarian reserve has a baseline day 3 FSH of 18 IU/L and an AMH of 0.2 ng/mL. She fails multiple stimulation cycles with poor oocyte yield. What option offers her the highest cumulative live birth rate per cycle?
o: In vitro fertilization using donor oocytes
Repeat IVF with ultra-high dose gonadotropins
items.exp: In women with advanced reproductive age and severely diminished ovarian reserve (AMH < 0.5 ng/mL, baseline FSH > 15-20 IU/L), autologous oocyte IVF yields live birth rates < 5%. In vitro fertilization using donor oocytes from young fertile donors confers live birth rates > 50% per transfer, reflecting the donor's age.
r: Correct. Donor oocyte IVF provides the highest live birth rate (> 50%) because embryo quality depends primarily on oocyte age.
Incorrect. High-dose gonadotropins cannot recruit non-existent follicles in severely depleted ovaries.
Incorrect. Natural cycle IUI has a negligible success rate in severe DOR.
Incorrect. Ovarian wedge resection destroys remaining ovarian tissue and accelerates premature ovarian failure.
items.kp: Donor oocyte IVF provides the highest live birth rate in women with severe diminished ovarian reserve.
